source:
You are an expert Roblox game developer, technical artist, and sound designer. Build a complete, playable Roblox turn-based single-player JRPG inspired by the systems and feel of Final Fantasy X - a story-driven pilgrimage across a linear-but-lush world, with strategic turn-based combat. Use ONLY original world, characters, names, and lore (no Square Enix IP, no Spira/Tidus/Yuna/blitzball or other protected assets). It should look and play well on ALL platforms: phone, tablet, PC, and console.

FIRST: produce a full Game Design Document (GDD) - game pillars and vision, target audience, core loop, an original setting and cast (a doomed-world pilgrimage premise in the spirit of FFX but wholly original), the combat system design, party/character-role design, progression grid, ability/magic system, world/zone structure, side activities (an original minigame in the spirit of blitzball), economy, art and audio direction, UI/UX and cross-platform input strategy, monetization philosophy (cosmetic-only, no pay-to-win), and success metrics. THEN produce a detailed technical implementation plan - architecture, module breakdown, instance hierarchy, data flow, save system, and milestone order. THEN autonomously implement the entire plan end to end without waiting for further input: write all scripts, build/define all systems, wire everything up, author a vertical-slice's worth of content (intro zone, first town, first dungeon, a boss, a starting party), and deliver a working, good-looking, good-sounding playable slice.

CORE COMBAT (the FFX feel - CTB, not real-time)
- Conditional Turn-Based (CTB) system: turn order is an explicit, visible timeline driven by each combatant's Speed and each action's recovery cost. Fast actions grant sooner next-turns; heavy actions push you back. Show the upcoming turn-order queue on-screen and let it update dynamically as haste/slow/actions change.
- Full pause-to-think: no ATB clock pressure - the game waits for input. Deep, deliberate, readable.
- Free mid-battle party swapping: a roster where you can sub any benched member in on your turn, so encounters reward using the whole party. Each character/role counters specific enemy types (armored, agile, flying, magical, tanky) so swapping is the strategic core.
- Command menu: Attack, Skill/Ability, Magic, Item, Defend, Swap, Flee. Elemental and status affinities (fire/ice/lightning/water, poison/slow/silence/petrify/sleep). Overdrive-style limit meter that builds from taking/dealing damage and unleashes powerful signature moves.
- Summon-style mechanic (original): call a powerful guardian entity that replaces the party temporarily with its own turn, health, and overdrive. Original creatures only.

PARTY & PROGRESSION
- A small cast of distinct roles: e.g. a balanced striker, an armor-breaker, an agile multi-hitter, a black-magic caster, a white-magic healer, a status/utility specialist, and a heavy hitter - each best against certain foes.
- A Sphere-Grid-style progression board (original design): a large shared node network where characters spend earned points to move across nodes unlocking stats and abilities, with branching paths and gates that let builds diverge and eventually cross into other roles. No linear levels - growth is spatial and player-directed.
- Equipment with ability slots/affinities rather than raw tiers; customization over stat-inflation.

WORLD & CONTENT
- Linear-but-rich zone progression: a sequence of handcrafted, atmospheric regions connected as a pilgrimage toward a distant goal, each with a distinct biome, town/save points, NPCs, treasure, and a set-piece boss.
- Save spheres/points that heal and save. World map as a stylized route between zones.
- An original side minigame in the spirit of blitzball (e.g. an arena sport or strategic mini-competition) with its own rules, recruitable players, and rewards.
- Sidequests, an optional superboss, and collectible ability items. Vertical slice must include: opening cinematic-lite intro, first town, first field zone, first dungeon, first boss, and a working sphere-grid + CTB battle loop.

VISUAL QUALITY (painterly, cinematic JRPG - not default Roblox)
- Lush, atmospheric, emotionally-toned art direction: stylized-realistic environments, strong sense of place and scale, volumetric light shafts, water and reflections, gentle fog for depth. Each zone a distinct palette and mood (sun-drenched coast, solemn temple, storm-lit ruin).
- Lighting: Future lighting, Bloom + ColorCorrection + SunRays + DepthOfField, per-zone color grade; dramatic key light in cutscenes and boss reveals.
- Materials & maps: cohesive stylized PBR, clean readable silhouettes, hero lighting on save points, chests, and story NPCs. Skyboxes + atmospheric haze. No flat untextured parts.
- Battle presentation: distinct battle camera with dynamic angles per action, spell VFX (elemental particles + light + screen tint), physical-hit impact frames and hit-stop, summon entrance set-piece, overdrive flourish. Damage numbers, status icons, clean turn-order timeline UI.
- Camera & feel: smooth exploration follow-cam, cinematic framing in scripted moments, subtle shake on big hits, slow-mo on finishing blows.
- UI: elegant, diegetic-leaning JRPG menus - command ring/list, ATB-free turn timeline, party status bars, sphere grid board, menu with equip/abilities/items - animated, legible, no clutter.
- Performance: pool VFX, LOD, stream zones, hold 60fps.

SOUND DESIGN (orchestral, emotional, reactive)
- Music: sweeping original orchestral/ambient score - a wistful main theme, per-zone exploration tracks, a driving battle theme, a boss theme, a victory fanfare, an emotional story motif. Adaptive layers for tension and triumph. Diegetic UI plips.
- SFX: menu cursor/confirm/cancel, spell and physical-hit sounds by element/type, status-effect cues, summon roar, save-point shimmer, chest jingle, level/grid-node unlock chime. 3D positional world SFX (water, wind, town bustle, dungeon drips).
- Mixing: SoundGroups for Music/SFX/UI/Ambience with ducking under fanfares and cutscene lines. Reverb zones (temple vs. open coast). Per-zone ambient beds. Master + per-bus volume in settings.
- Optional lightweight voice-bark support (hooks for VO on key lines) even if placeholder.

MOBILE & CROSS-PLATFORM (must play well on phone/tablet/console, not just PC)
- Detect input type and adapt: touch, mouse/keyboard, and gamepad all first-class. Never assume PC. Turn-based combat suits touch well - lean into clean tappable menus.
- Touch controls: tap-to-select command menus and targets, virtual stick for field movement, tap-to-move option, large legible battle command UI, swipe/tap navigation of the sphere grid.
- Auto-scaling UI: Scale-based UDim2 + anchor points so battle menus, turn timeline, and grid board reflow for phone, tablet, and TV-safe zones. Large, thumb-reachable targets.
- Adaptive quality tiers: auto-detect device power and scale particles, dynamic lights, bloom/DOF, reflections, and draw distance down on mobile to hold 60fps (30fps floor). Manual quality toggle.
- Camera: touch-drag/right-stick orbit in field; full gamepad menu navigation and cursor memory.
- Test every system against touch and gamepad, not just PC input.

TECH
- Luau, server-authoritative saves and progression (grid nodes, inventory, story flags, party); combat can resolve client-side with server validation of rewards to prevent exploits. No client-trusted currency, items, or grid points. DataStore-backed saves with session locking and autosave at save points.
- Modular: CTBBattleSystem (turn-order timeline engine), CommandMenu, PartyManager (swap/roster), AbilityMagicSystem, StatusEffectSystem, SummonSystem, SphereGridProgression, InventoryEquipSystem, EnemyAI (role/affinity-aware), ZoneStreamingManager, DialogueCutsceneManager, MinigameManager, SaveManager, VFXManager, AudioManager, CameraController, InputManager (cross-platform), UI. Clean RemoteEvents/RemoteFunctions and data-driven definitions (abilities, enemies, items, grid nodes as data tables/ModuleScripts so content is easy to expand).
- Data-driven content pipeline so new zones, enemies, abilities, and grid nodes are authored as config, not hardcoded.

Deliver in this order: (1) the GDD, (2) the technical implementation plan, (3) all commented scripts, the folder/instance hierarchy, data-definition modules, and VFX/lighting/audio setup, (4) setup steps and how to add new content. Implement the code in order: CTB battle core + turn-order timeline (get the combat feel right first) → command menu, party swap, abilities/magic/status → sphere-grid progression + equipment → enemy AI & a boss → zone streaming, save points & exploration → dialogue/cutscene + one story beat → the original side minigame → cross-platform input & UI scaling. Build a polished vertical slice, keep everything data-driven for expansion, and work autonomously through every milestone until the slice looks, sounds, and plays great on every device.

answers.ask: How many zones should the pilgrimage have, and how long should one take to walk end to end?
answers.answer: For the playable vertical slice, build three traversable zones: the first town, first field, and first dungeon; each should take roughly 3–5 minutes to walk end to end, with the dungeon slightly more compact and encounter-focused.

answers.ask: Is the route strictly linear, or can the party walk back to earlier zones?
answers.answer: Use a strictly linear forward route for the slice, with a stylized world-map route that unlocks the next zone after its objective is complete; no backtracking is needed.

config.evidence: “turn-based single-player JRPG,” “Linear-but-rich zone progression,” and “a sequence of handcrafted... regions connected as a pilgrimage,” with “first town, first field zone, first dungeon” support a contiguous town/road/clearing world rather than a hub-to-instanced-dungeons structure.
config.addendum:
LAYOUT FEATURES for this RPG map. Build these as the actual structure of the space rather than as set dressing, keep them visually distinct from one another, and keep the whole layout legible in one view.

SHAPE OF THE SPACE - Single Contiguous Map: Town, roads, and mob clearings all on one surface, no instanced areas.

INCLUDE:
- Sanctuary Town: A settlement completely isolated from enemy AI where players restock, repair, and turn in quests.
- Level-Gated Throat: Highly visible blockades — guarded bridges, castle gates, mountain cracks — physically stopping under-levelled players entering high-threat ground.
